text.p: These are the leading stories in Bosnian press on Wednesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch fo their accuracy.

- Bosnia and the London Club of creditors concluded an agreement on restructuring the country's $1.4 billion debt. Co-chairman of the Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, says the deal is a result of successful negotiations with commercial banks, which showed an understanding for extensive damage caused by the war.

- Robert Gelbard, special U.S. envoy to Bosnia, says the next step following the agreement with the London Club should be a signing of a letter of intent with the International Monetary Fund. This would clear the way for donors' conference in the second half of July.

- During a visit to Mostar, Gelbard requested from Croatian Democratic Union to implement all agreements related to status of Mostar within 24 hours. Otherwise, Washington will cut off economic aid to Bosnian Croats who lost their creditbility as negotiating partners due to their habit of breaking promises, Gelbard said.
- There was no agreement on formation of a joint police force in Mostar on Tuesday, because the Croats still insisted that a national composition of force should reflect a current situation.

- President of Bosnia's Serb entity, Biljana Plavsic, in televised speech accuses interior minister Dragan Kijac of allowing illegal smuggling operations. Kijac said ex-president and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic approved the smuggling deals, Plavsic said.

- Moslem-Croat federation minister of agriculture and forestry, Ahmed Smajic, said wood mills are working illegally and making big profits on wood exports to Croatia without paying taxes. In the federation, there are 1,600 mills and most of the firms have not registered. The government plans to discuss how to regulate the industry, he said. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
